_doc: Hardee's Rifle and Light Infantry Tactics (War Department, adopted 29 March 1855; cited from the Richmond 1861 printing, vol. 1 Schools of the Soldier and Company and Instruction for Skirmishers, vol. 2 School of the Battalion, with the Memphis 1861 one-volume printing as a second OCR witness) and the passages of Casey's Infantry Tactics (1862) that are set against it in drill_compare.json. Same method as drill_infantry.json: manual id, printed page (from OCR running heads, confidence stated), verbatim OCR phrase (<15 words) checked by tools/bt/drill_check.py, own-words paraphrase. Items are tier=documented (primary manual text, OCR-verified); the OCR is raw and uncorrected, no page image was inspected.

scope_note: Hardee citations are from HARDEE-1861b (Richmond 1861, legible running heads); HARDEE-1861a (Memphis 1861) is the second witness (witness_a: the longest run of the phrase found verbatim there); Casey is cited from drill_infantry.json (INF-*) or the HCS-* items here.
edition_note: HARDEE-1861b and HARDEE-1861a are two 1861 printings of the same 1855 text; the paragraph numbers agree (Load in nine times = No. 156 in both contents lists). Casey renumbers: Casey S.S. = Hardee + 7 (to Hardee 186 = Casey 193), + 9 after the inserted paras 194-195.

load_in_nine_times.where: School of the Soldier, Part II, Lesson II, paras 156-170
load_in_nine_times.note: Same nine commands, same order and motions as Casey (paras 163-177); CMP-S02 records the one difference of substance (rifle-musket variant).

load_in_eight_times.note: Maynard-primer variant, printed as a footnote in Hardee.

rate_of_fire.finding: Only a training standard: every man able to load and fire at least three rounds a minute with ease and regularity (S.C. para 47), identical to Casey; manual-of-arms motions are timed at 1/90 minute except the cartridge, rammer and bayonet motions. No combat rate is printed.

misfire.finding: Procedure only: pick and prime again if no smoke escapes on uncocking, judge a double charge by the height of the load, ball screw for three cartridges, new cap when the tube is stopped, spring the rammer to learn whether a piece discharged. No misfire rate.

rate_misfire_cartridge_range.fouling: No statement (regex count 0 in both Hardee printings and both Casey volumes).
rate_misfire_cartridge_range.cartridge_and_buck_and_ball: Only the loading motions describe the cartridge (tear the paper, empty the powder, insert the ball point up); no powder charge, ball, weight or buckshot is printed in Hardee or Casey (regex counts 0). The buck-and-ball description is in the Ordnance Manual (drill_infantry.json INF-AMMO-01).
rate_misfire_cartridge_range.effective_range: None printed. The only yard figures are marching rates (negative_findings).

hardee_general_bugle_calls.note: Listed 1-25 in the OCR (call numbers partly garbled; the last is School call). The musical notation is not in the OCR text.

hardee_skirmisher_bugle_calls.note: Numbers 1-4 and 6-23 are in the OCR; call 5 is missing (Casey's call 5 is The run).

bugle_and_drum_calls.casey_extra: Casey has one more general bugle call (Signal of execution), the drum beats (15 general, 20 skirmisher) and the drum-major's staff signals; Hardee has none of these in either printing (CMP-L01, L04, L05).

skirmisher_instruction.structure: General principles (Nos. 1-14); Article First deployments (15-69); Article Second marches (70-105); Article Third firings (106-126); Article Fourth the rally (127-177); Article Fifth deploy the battalion (178-197); then the sabre manual, salute of the color, relieving sentinels, parade rest and the bugle calls.

usage_1863.question: Which manual did each army use in 1863?

union.verdict: PARTLY ESTABLISHED: the War Department adopted Casey for all infantry (regular, volunteer, militia) on 11 August 1862; whether each regiment had switched by July 1863 is not stated in these texts
union.caveat: The order says Casey is "adopted"; Casey's own preface says Scott's and Hardee's systems had both been in use. The only regimental statement in the downloaded texts is the 44th NY anecdote (one regiment).

confederate.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED by the manuals or the other downloaded texts
confederate.caveat: The Hardee printings are Richmond (J. W. Randolph) and Memphis imprints dated 1861, and the order they reprint is the US War Department order of 29 March 1855 limited to light infantry and riflemen. A Southern printing shows the book was produced there in 1861, not that every Confederate regiment used it in 1863. Battles and Leaders vol. 3, the three OR vol. 27 parts and the state Gettysburg volumes contain no statement naming either manual (search recorded in usage_search).

negative_findings.claim: Hardee and Casey never mention buck and ball, buckshot or the buck-and-ball cartridge
Hardee and Casey never mention fouling
Neither manual gives an effective range or a firing distance in yards (the only yard figures are marching rates)
The only yard figures in Hardee are two marching rates (4,000 yards in about 25 minutes at double quick; about 1,100 yards in 7 minutes)
Neither manual describes the cartridge beyond the loading motions (no powder charge, weight or ball size)
The words "missed fire" occur exactly once in each of Hardee (both printings) and Casey vol. 1 (S.C. para 83); no other drill passage uses them and no misfire rate is given
Casey vol. 2 (School of the Battalion) has no passage on misfires
